label: 0055 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 53 windows): 0053 with the 30 km BEL sheet uncut, reaching the Japan Trench beneath the forearc as one sheet, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0053 on a base whose 30 km BEL sheet is no longer cut beneath the Japan Trench forearc. It reaches the trench as one mesh with one prior (3,895 triangles, 932 modes), so the BEL's afterslip states and its field in each window cover the forearc. Beneath the offshore forearc the flat sheet lies inside the subducting plate; beneath the coast it hangs over the slab. After Tohoku the BEL slips 80–100 mm/yr beneath the forearc off Miyagi. The seafloor fit matches 0052's (28 and 48 mm), and the onshore fit after Tohoku is 0.7% better than 0053's. But the shallow megathrust off Miyagi then shows ongoing afterslip, with coupling 0.28 on average in 2012–2021, instead of relocking: the sheet trades with megathrust afterslip, as the uncut BEL did before it was cut. Held-out data are predicted worse: seafloor cross-validation is +1,037 and onshore window cross-validation −1,684, against +1,138 and +548 for 0054. The losses are spread over the windows after Tohoku. The same sheet at 20 km scores lower still (−3,428) and isn't shown.
